result:
**Assumption:** I take the original three-place knot to be not-all-equal (NAE), with stabilizer G = {000, 111}. All of the below is derived by hand, with nothing run.

| Scope | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Four requirements force the rule | Fails | Every signed or dephased rival built from a positive-semidefinite preparation passes agreement, multiplication and no-signalling automatically. Certain plus is exactly "sign constant on G-orbits", so testing it on those rivals is vacuous. If G is trivial, the plain mixture with no second-question content passes all four. |
| Signed rivals on the knot | Not rivals | Conjugating by a parity question Z_V with V orthogonal to G fixes every parity answer and renames flip answers by (−1)^{V·T}. On NAE the four orbit-constant sign patterns are exactly the four such V, so a "rejection" there is a naming convention. Only non-character signs are real rivals, and they need a larger S. |
| Dephasing rival insensitive to renaming | Survives | Mixing across G-orbits is the uniform average of those renamed rivals, so any requirement linear in probabilities that they pass, it passes. Only a non-linear requirement (no finer preparation) or the rule itself removes it, and the second is circular. |
| Pair-conditional uniqueness | Weaker than stated | Exposing the pair of x→x+T dephases across pairs, and every Z_U disjoint from T is constant on a pair. So a rival coherent only within T-pairs reproduces the whole rule at that T, and "change marginal unchanged" holds for every rival. The discriminating content is consistency across different T: one multiplicative renaming for all T, not a sign per question. |
| Six-rule game | Gap | In the literature's Mermin–Peres square, the third real product has overlapping flip and parity sets. The disjoint rule is silent there, and its minus sign comes from ordering, not pair counting. "No signed weights" is true of the preparation but not of the question. |
| K2 quantifiers | Mismatch | K2 is ∀∃ on allowed states and weighting-free. Certain plus is ∀x, a positive score is ∃x, and its value is a fraction under the uniform weighting. NAE passes K2, yet flipping one bit scores 4/6. Any positive reweighting keeps K1–K3 and changes every score. |
| Projection vs whole-input flip | Not equivalent | Projecting a birth onto its inputs is full at every arity. Flipping all k inputs commutes with the closing parity only for even k; at odd k it scores exactly 0 unless the born variable is flipped too. Even k still fails on older constraints: flipping 110 on NAE scores 4/6 while the projection is full. |
| Fade or return | Explainable at all sizes | The score is the paired fraction, |S∩(S+T)|/|S| at U = ∅. Parity-only stages give exactly 0 or ±1, so nothing fades there. A birth with odd overlap with T kills the score permanently. A birth that deletes unpaired words raises it: adding x2≠x3 to NAE lifts flip-100 from 4/6 to 1. A birth with even overlap that depends on nothing else leaves it unchanged. Any other return means forgetting, a redefined T, or censoring. |

**Next step:** Before measuring, quotient rivals by the Z_V renamings and write down the one requirement that is not linear in probabilities.

| Direction | Payoff | Concreteness |
|---|---|---|
| Test non-character signs on a stabilizer-free S with dependent words, e.g. {000,100,010,001,111} with 111 negated; T = 011 then shows both signs | 2 | 3 |
| Pre-register the kill/raise/unchanged law above as the all-size prediction | 3 | 2 |
| Report censored stages as bounds in [−1,1], not the mean of survivors; a birth that enlarges a stage may also kill its score | 2 | 3 |

**Corrections:** none; nothing left a session.
**Goals:** none moved.
**Assumptions:** none recorded; this is advice only.
**Scaffolds:** none recorded. If the study proceeds, three need entries: the uniform weighting, "same T" as the followed question, and the overlap sign convention. Each needs a test under another choice.
